name: CONGO
lead: Congo is in the middle of Africa. Thick rainforest covers it. Gorillas, forest elephants and thousands of birds live there. Brazzaville, the capital, is on the Congo River. Kinshasa, in DR Congo, is just 4 km across the water.
geo: Forests cover about 65% of Congo. They are part of the world's second-largest tropical rainforest. The Congo River carries more water than any other river except the Amazon.
The Congo River forms the eastern border. It is so deep that its fish have evolved to be blind. In the west, the Crystal Mountains drop to the Atlantic coast.
animals: Western lowland gorillas live deep in Odzala-Kokoua National Park. Visitors can sit just metres from a male gorilla.
Forest elephants are smaller than grassland elephants, with rounder ears. They make clearings called bais. Over 400 bird species live here too.
culture: Congolese rumba mixes African Bantu rhythms, Cuban music and French ballroom dance. It swept the world in the 1950s. UNESCO (the UN's culture group) now recognises it.
People wear pagne (wax-print cloth) every day. The Sape movement is full of stylish men in designer suits.
history: Bantu-speaking peoples settled the Congo region over 2,000 years ago. In 1880, French explorer Pierre de Brazza signed a treaty with the Tio king. The capital was named after him.
In 1944, French leader de Gaulle held a key meeting in Brazzaville. It began to change France's ties with Africa. Congo became independent on 15 August 1960.
wows: Brazzaville and Kinshasa are the only capitals facing each other across a river, 4 km apart.
The Congo River is over 220 m deep, enough to hide a 20-storey building.
Congo's peat swamps hold about 30 billion tonnes of carbon, about 3 years of world coal and oil pollution.
Oil makes up about 89% of Congo's exports, though forest covers most land.
Odzala-Kokoua, protected since 1935, is one of Africa's oldest parks.
The Congo–Ocean Railway took 13 years to build by hand, finishing in 1934.
Nearly 70% of Congolese live in cities, despite the rainforest.

myths.myth: Congo and the DRC are one country
myths.fact: Two countries share the name. This one is smaller, on the west bank. The DR Congo is much bigger.

myths.myth: Gorillas beat their chests to attack
myths.fact: Chest-beating is a show to warn others. Gorillas are shy and eat mostly plants.
